turbulence

TUR-byuh-lens — think of a sputtering 'turbo' engine; turbulence is the rough, unsteady shaking of the ride. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Turbulence is violent or unsteady movement, especially in air or water.

The captain warned passengers to fasten their seatbelts before flying through an area of expected turbulence.

Example

A small boat crossing a calm lake suddenly hits a stretch of churning rapids, and the turbulence tosses and rocks it violently from side to side as the crew scrambles to hold on.

That violent, unsteady, unpredictable motion in the water is turbulence in its most literal form. Unlike 'current,' which just describes a steady flow, turbulence means rough, disordered movement.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

turmoil: Turmoil is great confusion and disturbance in human affairs — a family in turmoil, a company in turmoil, a country in turmoil. Turbulence begins as a physical word: violent, unsteady movement of air or water, borrowed only sometimes for stormy stretches of life.

agitation: Agitation is being stirred up — water sloshing in a machine, or a person shaking with nerves. It can be small and contained. Turbulence is bigger and wilder: whole stretches of air or water in violent, disordered motion, tossing whatever passes through.

choppiness: Choppiness is surface roughness — short, broken little waves that slap a boat around without real danger. Turbulence runs deeper and hits harder: violent, unsteady motion in air or water that can toss an aircraft or spin a raft without warning.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

calm: a state of stillness or peace

stability: the state of being steady and unchanging

Where it sits · how violently things are shaken up — unrest → turbulence → upheaval

unrest vs. turbulence: Unrest is weaker than turbulence in a physical sense — unrest often describes ongoing tension, while turbulence describes violent, immediate, physical shaking.

upheaval vs. turbulence: Upheaval sits above turbulence in force: turbulence shakes things violently, but an upheaval overturns them completely — a revolution, a lost job, a sudden move that turns a whole life or society upside down.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — turb-

root — turb-: to disturb, throw into disorder (Latin (turbare))

suffix — -ulence

suffix — -ulence: full of, state of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin turbare meant 'to disturb, throw into confusion,' related to turba, 'crowd, disorder.' Turbulence is, at its root, a state completely full of disturbance and disorder.

Use the root in a new word: disturb

Use the root in a new word: disturb: Astronomers spent a decade tracing what had perturbed the comet's orbit.
